title: Rome still titles dead faith saving/justifying as remote disposition
source_text: XXXIV. Imo quamvis fidem mortuam ad salutem nihil prodesse, & ad justitiam esse inutilem fateantur, quia neminem actu salvat & justificat, nihilominus illam ornant saepe titulo salvificae & justificantis, quoniam, remote saltem, hominem ad salutem & justitiam disponit. Et sic, secundum ipsos, fides salvifica atque justificans a charitate & bonis operibus separata existere potest.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed although they confess dead faith profits nothing for salvation and is useless for righteousness because it actually saves and justifies no one, nevertheless they often adorn it with the title of saving and justifying, because at least remotely it disposes a man to salvation and righteousness. And so, according to them, saving and justifying faith can exist separated from charity and good works.
pass_b_english: Rome admits dead faith does not actually save, yet still titles it saving/justifying as remote disposition.
On that naming, saving faith can exist apart from charity and works.

lemmas.gloss: with the title of saving and justifying
